Its README reports a 2026 example where pure RL improved Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on SWE-bench Verified from 47.8% to 61.6% with 1.8K training examples, and an Agent Lightning Skill that helps one coding agent improve another.
agent-lightning.who: ML engineers and researchers who want to improve an existing agent with RL instead of rebuilding it.
features: RL training with your agent's real harness
No rewrite of tools or control flow

long: Parlant is an interaction-control harness for customer-facing AI agents. The project says it is production-ready for enterprise B2C and sensitive B2B interactions that must be consistent, compliant, on-brand and traceable.
It positions itself as an open-source alternative to products like Ada, Decagon or Sierra, built around explicit behavior guidelines for conversational agents.
parlant.who: Teams building customer-facing chat agents that must follow rules reliably and stay on-brand.
features: For B2C and sensitive B2B use

long: OpenFang is an open-source Agent Operating System built in Rust, shipped as one binary. Its README cites 137K lines of code across 14 crates and 1,767+ tests.

It aims to be a full operating system for autonomous agents rather than a chatbot framework or multi-agent orchestrator. It is feature-complete but pre-1.0, so the maintainers advise pinning a commit for production.
openfang.who: Developers who want a self-contained runtime for autonomous agents and can handle pre-1.0 changes.
features: Agent OS in Rust, single binary

long: CAMEL is one of the first multi-agent frameworks, for building role-playing agents and large agent societies. It is run by an open-source community dedicated to finding the scaling laws of agents by studying them at large scale.
camel.who: Researchers and developers exploring multi-agent role-play and large agent populations.

long: AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications, integrating agents, real-time user context and user interfaces.
You can build AG-UI-powered apps or new framework integrations from quickstarts, and try examples in the AG-UI Dojo.
ag-ui.who: Developers connecting agent backends to frontends who want a standard way to stream agent state and events.
features: Agent-to-UI streaming of state and events

long: Trigger.dev is an open-source platform for building AI agents and workflows in TypeScript, with long-running tasks, retries, queues, observability and elastic scaling.
You build agents with the frameworks, services and LLMs you already use and deploy them to Trigger.dev for durable execution. It can be self-hosted or used as a managed cloud.
trigger-dev.who: TypeScript developers who need durable background jobs and agents that can run for a long time and retry safely.

long: Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) is an open, multi-language framework for building production-grade AI agents and multi-agent workflows in .NET and Python.

It aims to give teams moving from prototype to production a consistent foundation for building, orchestrating and operating agents, and supports Microsoft Foundry, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI and the GitHub Copilot SDK.
microsoft-agent-framework.who: Enterprise teams on .NET or Python, especially in the Microsoft and Azure ecosystem.
features: Microsoft Foundry, Azure OpenAI and OpenAI support

long: PocketFlow is a minimalist LLM framework in 100 lines, with zero dependencies and no vendor lock-in. It still supports agents, multi-agent setups, workflows and RAG.
Its makers encourage agentic coding, letting AI agents such as Cursor build agents with it, and ports exist for TypeScript, Java and other languages. You can install it or simply copy the source.
pocketflow.who: Developers who want to understand and control every line of their LLM framework.

long: Tambo is an open-source generative UI toolkit for React: connect your components and Tambo handles streaming, state management and MCP so agents can render them.
Note: Tambo Cloud is shutting down. New signups are closed, the hosted API stops on October 31, 2026, and user data is deleted on November 30, 2026. The open-source toolkit remains self-hostable.
tambo.who: React developers who want agents to render real UI components and are comfortable self-hosting.

long: Aden Hive is an open-source runtime for colonies of AI agents that do real business work. You tell a queen agent what you need; she does the first piece herself to learn the job, then hands the rest to parallel workers.
Every result lands in a shared tracker you can query, audit and resume from.
aden-hive.who: Teams who want to split business research or operations tasks across many parallel agents with an audit trail.

long: Spring AI Alibaba is a production-ready Java framework, built on Spring AI, for building agentic, workflow and multi-agent applications.

Its agent framework has built-in context engineering and human-in-the-loop support, and Spring AI Alibaba Admin is an agent platform for visual agent development, observability, evaluation and MCP management that can migrate Dify DSL projects.
spring-ai-alibaba.who: Java and Spring developers building agents and workflows.
features: Java agent framework on Spring AI
Context engineering and human in the loop
Admin platform with observability and evals

long: Omnigent is an open-source meta-harness that gives you one orchestration layer over Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Hermes, Pi and agents you write yourself.
You can swap or combine harnesses without rewriting, enforce policies and sandboxing, and collaborate in real time from the terminal, browser, phone or a native macOS desktop app.
omnigent.who: Developers and teams using several agent harnesses who want shared policies and one place to run them.
features: One layer over many agent harnesses
Works from terminal, browser, phone or desktop

long: VoltAgent is an AI agent engineering platform with two parts: an open-source TypeScript framework (memory, RAG, guardrails, tools, MCP, voice and workflows) and the VoltOps Console for observability, automation, deployment, evals and prompts.
The console is available in the cloud or self-hosted, and the framework connects to any AI provider.
voltagent.who: TypeScript developers who want a framework plus an operations console for their agents.
features: TypeScript framework with memory, RAG, tools and MCP

long: OpenPipe makes reinforcement-learning tooling for training better agents, including the open-source ART library for training multi-step agents on real-world tasks with GRPO.
Its README also describes W&B Training (Serverless RL), a hosted service that manages training and inference infrastructure so you focus on data, environment and reward function.
openpipe.who: ML engineers who want to train agents with RL without building the training infrastructure themselves.
features: ART library for multi-step agent RL (GRPO)

long: PraisonAI is a multi-agent framework for building a self-improving AI workforce with little code. Its makers say agents that research, plan and execute tasks across your apps can be deployed in five lines.
It covers several layers of the agent stack, from one agent to a whole organization, including where the agent runs.
praisonai.who: Developers who want to stand up multi-agent automations quickly with minimal code.
features: Research, planning and execution across apps

long: Strands Agents is an open-source SDK for building and running AI agents in Python and TypeScript with a model-driven approach. It runs in your process with no hosted control plane.
One SDK covers lifecycle controls (turn limits, token budgets, cancellation), tools and structured output, MCP, multi-agent patterns, memory and sessions, model portability and streaming.
strands-agents.who: Developers who would otherwise write their own agent loop and want the common pieces ready-made.
features: Turn limits, token budgets and cancellation

long: Evolver is a self-evolving engine for AI agents built around auditable genes, capsules and events. It has been open source since February 2026 (MIT, then GPL-3.0-or-later from April 2026).
Its README announces that future releases will move toward source-available licensing, so check the current license before adopting it.
evolver.who: Developers experimenting with agents that evolve their own skills and memory, who want an audit trail of changes.
features: Self-evolution with auditable genes and capsules

long: Upsonic is a Python framework for building autonomous agents, similar in spirit to OpenClaw or Claude Cowork, as well as more traditional agent systems.

File and shell operations are restricted to a workspace, with path traversal and dangerous commands blocked, and the community publishes prebuilt agents. Its docs are available as an llms.txt source for coding tools.
upsonic.who: Python developers building autonomous agents who want workspace restrictions built in.

long: Agent Squad is a lightweight open-source framework for orchestrating multiple AI agents, in the cloud with Python and TypeScript and on device with Swift.

It routes conversations to specialized agents, and offers a classifier that routes with a decision model instead of an LLM. The Swift version runs agents, MCP tools, realtime voice and tracing entirely on iPhone, iPad and Mac.
agent-squad.who: Developers who need to route user conversations across several specialized agents, including on Apple devices.
features: Multi-agent routing in Python and TypeScript

long: Flyte is a type-safe orchestration platform for ML pipelines, models and agents at scale, in pure Python, running on Kubernetes. It is a graduated project of the LF AI & Data Foundation.
Flyte 2 can be tried locally with a devbox, and a TUI provides a local development experience; Flyte 1 is maintained on a separate branch.
flyte.who: ML and data teams who orchestrate pipelines and agents on Kubernetes.
features: Pipelines, models and agents in pure Python

long: OpenEvolve is an open-source evolutionary coding agent inspired by AlphaEvolve. It turns LLMs into autonomous code optimizers that evolve better code and algorithms.
Its README reports 2-3x speedups on real hardware and state-of-the-art results on problems such as circle packing.
openevolve.who: Researchers and engineers who want to search for faster or better algorithms automatically.

long: Swarms is a multi-agent orchestration framework that its makers describe as enterprise-grade and production-ready. You build, deploy and scale multi-agent systems in Python.
It includes harnesses for sequential, concurrent and hierarchical architectures and integrates with MCP, x402 and skills. An optional fast extra adds a drop-in LLM gateway for faster model calls.
swarms.who: Python developers building multi-agent systems with standard architectures such as hierarchies.

long: Agent-Native is Builder.io's open-source TypeScript framework for agents that come with their own app UI. You define each capability once as an action: the agent uses it as a tool and the UI calls it from code.
Our listing notes the same action is shared by the UI, agent, API, CLI, MCP and A2A, and that hosted building on Builder.io is optional.
agent-native-builder-io.who: TypeScript developers building agent products that need a purpose-built interface, not just a chat box.
features: Actions shared by agent and UI
Exposed via API, CLI, MCP and A2A

long: Open Multi-Agent (OMA) is a self-hosted TypeScript agent runtime. Consequential actions wait for durable, tamper-evident approvals, and every run leaves a record you can verify offline.
There is no telemetry and no hosted control plane. You use your own keys and models, cloud or local (Ollama, vLLM, llama-server). It needs Node.js 20 or newer.
open-multi-agent.who: Organizations that need agents they can own, approve and audit on their own infrastructure.

long: Julep builds AI agents as composable, durable dataflows rather than ad-hoc loops. Flows can crash and resume, retry safely, explain every step, and deny any tool the model was not explicitly allowed to call.
The main authoring style is a Python @flow, where ordinary Python names graph steps such as tools, reasoners, branches, fan-out and retries. A cloud option is available.
julep.who: Python developers who need reliable, explainable agent workflows that survive crashes.
features: Durable flows that resume after crashes

long: Genkit is Google's open-source framework for building full-stack AI-powered applications, built and used in production by Firebase.
SDKs cover JavaScript/TypeScript and Go (production-ready), Python (beta) and Dart (preview), with a unified interface across models.
genkit.who: App developers, especially on Firebase or Google Cloud, adding AI and agent features in JS, Go, Python or Dart.

long: IntentKit is an open-source, self-hosted cloud agent cluster that manages a collaborating team of AI agents for you.
It takes the cloud-native path rather than local-first: agents run in the cloud with minimal local resources and little maintenance.
intentkit.who: Teams who want a team of agents running on their own cloud infrastructure rather than on a laptop.

long: TrueForge, from TrueFoundry, is an open-source agent harness: the runtime layer that turns an LLM into a working agent. It runs the execution loop, including model calls, MCP tools, skills, sandboxing, approvals, context management and session state.
It exposes the agent three ways: a chat UI, an HTTP API with a TypeScript SDK, and an embeddable UI SDK.
trueforge.who: Developers who want streaming, persistence, tool servers, sandboxing and approvals without building the runtime themselves.
features: Managed agent loop with MCP tools and skills
Chat UI, HTTP API and TypeScript SDK

long: Marvin is a Python framework from Prefect for producing structured outputs and building agentic AI workflows.

You can cast, classify, extract and generate structured data, define observable tasks, assign specialized agents to them and combine tasks into threads. It uses OpenAI by default and can be configured for other providers.
marvin.who: Python developers who need structured LLM outputs and simple task-based agent workflows.

long: AgentScope Java 2.0 is a production-ready framework for building distributed, enterprise-grade agents in Java, with support for long-running, safely controlled execution.

It includes a unified event stream with 32 typed events for frontend rendering and human-in-the-loop, a permission system that can allow, require approval for or deny tool calls, and AOP-style middleware hooks.
agentscope-java.who: Java teams building enterprise agents that need permissions and event streams.
features: 32 typed events for UIs and human in the loop

long: Open Agents is Vercel's open-source reference app for building and running background coding agents on Vercel. It includes the web UI, agent runtime, sandbox orchestration and GitHub integration needed to go from prompt to code changes without your laptop.
The agent runs as a durable workflow on Vercel, and the repo is meant to be forked and adapted.
open-agents.who: Developers who want a starting point for their own cloud coding agent on Vercel.
features: Web UI with auth, sessions and streaming

long: Cloudflare Agents is Cloudflare's SDK for persistent, stateful AI agents powered by Durable Objects. Each agent has its own state, storage and lifecycle, with built-in real-time communication, scheduling, AI model calls, MCP and workflows.
Agents hibernate when idle and wake on demand, so you can run very many of them, one per user, session or game room, at no cost while inactive.
cloudflare-agents.who: Developers deploying agents on Cloudflare Workers who need per-user state at scale.

long: AReaL is a large-scale asynchronous reinforcement-learning system for training LLM-based agents, originally developed by Tsinghua IIIS and the AReaL team at Ant Group.
It is built on a fully asynchronous RL training paradigm optimized for efficiency and scalability.
areal.who: ML researchers and engineers training agentic models with RL at scale.

long: ZenML is built for ML and AI engineers working on traditional ML, LLM workflows or agents in a company setting. At its core you write workflows (pipelines) that can be run and tracked.
Our listing describes it as an MLOps and agent platform for building pipelines and deploying agents, with a cloud option.
zenml.who: ML and AI engineering teams that want reproducible pipelines for models and agents.
features: Pipelines for ML, LLM and agent workflows

long: AG2 is the community continuation of AutoGen, an open-source framework for multi-agent systems. As of AG2 v1.0, a protocol-driven framework is the top-level package, imported as ag2.
The classic framework (ConversableAgent, GroupChat, import autogen) moved to the ag2-classic repository, which is still maintained and installable.
ag2.who: Developers building multi-agent systems, including former AutoGen users.

long: Prime Intellect builds decentralized compute and an open RL environment hub for training agentic models. Its open-source verifiers library creates environments to train and evaluate LLMs.
verifiers is integrated with the Environments Hub, the prime-rl training framework and a Hosted Training platform, and the Prime CLI is recommended for working with environments.
prime-intellect.who: ML researchers who build RL environments and train or evaluate agentic models.

long: Koog is JetBrains' framework for building and running AI agents in idiomatic Kotlin and Java. Agents can use tools, handle complex workflows and talk with users.
It supports Kotlin Multiplatform deployment to JVM, JS, WasmJS, Android and iOS, and offers reliability features such as built-in retries and agent persistence to restore state at specific points.
koog.who: Kotlin and Java developers building predictable agents for the JVM and mobile.

long: Docker Agent lets you build, run and share AI agents with a declarative YAML config, a rich tool ecosystem and multi-agent orchestration, without writing code.
It is a Docker CLI plugin run as docker agent, and you can create teams of specialized agents that delegate tasks automatically.
docker-agent.who: Developers who already use Docker and want to define agents in YAML.

long: Agent Service Toolkit is a full toolkit for running an AI agent service built with LangGraph, FastAPI and Streamlit. It includes a LangGraph agent, a FastAPI service, a client and a Streamlit chat app, with Pydantic data structures and settings.
It is a template that shows a complete setup from agent definition to user interface.
agent-service-toolkit.who: Python developers who want a ready-made template for serving LangGraph agents.

long: Embabel (pronounced Em-BAY-bel) is a framework for authoring agentic flows on the JVM. Our listing notes it comes from the creator of Spring.
embabel.who: JVM developers, particularly Spring users, building agent flows.

long: RubyLLM is a Ruby framework for building AI features the Ruby way, with models, tools, agents, sandboxed code, evaluations and Rails conventions under one consistent API.
You can move between hosted and local providers without rewriting your application, or connect an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
rubyllm.who: Ruby and Rails developers adding chat, tools and agents to their apps.
features: One API for chat, tools and agents

long: Dagu is a local-first, open-source workflow engine for operations and internal automation. It is a single binary with a built-in web UI and no external database or message broker, running on Linux, macOS and Windows.
You define DAGs in YAML; it supports shell commands, Docker containers, Kubernetes Jobs and SSH, and turns scripts and runbooks into scheduled workflows with retries and human tasks.
dagu.who: Ops and platform engineers who want a simple self-hosted scheduler, including for agent jobs.

long: DocETL, from UC Berkeley, helps you process large collections of structured and unstructured data with LLMs. You write each operation in natural language, such as pulling every complaint out of a ticket.

It provides operators like map, reduce and filter, parallelizes work across your data and optimizes the pipeline automatically by swapping models, rewriting prompts and decomposing operations. It has a Python API, YAML and the DocWrangler UI.
docetl.who: Data and research teams running LLM-powered extraction over large document sets.
features: Python API, YAML and DocWrangler UI

long: Langroid is a lightweight, extensible Python framework for building LLM-powered applications, from researchers at CMU and UW-Madison. You set up agents, equip them with optional components such as an LLM, a vector store and tools, assign them tasks and have them collaborate.
Its maintainers note that pull requests are by invitation, for changes motivated by real use of Langroid in an organization.
langroid.who: Python developers who want a principled multi-agent framework built around agents and tasks.
features: Agents with optional LLM, vector store and tools

long: kagent is a Kubernetes-native framework for building AI agents. It makes it easy to build, deploy and manage agents inside Kubernetes, the most popular platform for running workloads.
Agents are its main building block, and the project aims to be easy to understand while still flexible.
kagent.who: Platform and DevOps teams that run on Kubernetes and want agents managed like other cluster workloads.

long: fast-agent is a flexible way to work with LLMs that can be used as a coding agent, development toolkit, evaluation tool or workflow platform. Our listing notes strong MCP, ACP and A2A support.

You can start an interactive session with shell support using uv, work with Hugging Face inference providers or an OpenAI Codex plan, and run shell commands from inside the session. Latest documentation is at fast-agent.ai.
fast-agent.who: Developers who want one tool to build, run and evaluate MCP-connected agents.
features: Coding agent, toolkit, evals and workflows
Hugging Face providers or Codex plan

long: LazyLLM is a low-code development tool for building multi-agent LLM applications. It helps developers create complex AI applications at low cost and keep optimizing them iteratively.
It provides a convenient application-building workflow plus standard processes and tools for the different stages of development.
lazyllm.who: Developers who want to assemble multi-agent LLM apps with little code.
features: Standard processes and tools per stage

long: TanStack AI is a type-safe, provider-agnostic TypeScript SDK for streaming chat, tool-calling agents, structured outputs, realtime voice and media generation.

It is built from composable activities and provider adapters, so you can use one provider or switch between many and import only what you need, such as chat, image, audio, transcription, realtime or devtools.
tanstack-ai.who: TypeScript developers who want type safety and provider freedom when building chat and agent features.
features: Chat, tools, structured output, voice and media

long: BotSharp is an open-source AI agent application framework for .NET that connects LLMs to your existing business applications.
The project describes itself as a toolkit for building conversation-as-a-platform bots, with natural-language understanding, computer vision and audio processing.
botsharp.who: .NET developers adding AI agents and bots to business systems.

long: Ax is a DSPy-style framework for building LLM programs and agents, TypeScript-first and published as @ax-llm/ax.

The same signatures, provider mappings, agents, flows, runtime contracts and optimizers are also compiled into generated Python, Java, C++, Go and Rust libraries, giving one programming model across languages.
ax.who: TypeScript developers (and polyglot teams) who like DSPy's signature-and-optimizer approach.
features: Generated libraries for Python, Java, C++, Go and Rust

long: RAGEN (Reasoning AGENT) is a flexible framework for training reasoning LLM agents with multi-turn reinforcement learning, built on the StarPO algorithm.
Its team also develops diagnostics to understand how agent RL training works and to fix hidden failure modes such as the "Echo Trap."
ragen.who: Researchers training multi-turn LLM agents with RL.

long: AgentField is an open-source control plane that lets you build AI agents callable by any service in your stack, like APIs, and run very many of them like microservices.
One request can fan out to thousands of agents while the control plane queues, retries and traces every branch. SDKs are available for Python, Go and TypeScript, plus a REST API.
agentfield.who: Backend teams that want agents to behave like scalable, observable services.
features: Fan-out with queues, retries and tracing

long: Agentic Context Engine (ACE) is an open-source engine that adds a persistent learning loop to AI agents, so they stop repeating mistakes and remember what worked.
ACE also powers Kayba, a managed service that handles the loop for you, from investigating failures to shipping fixes as pull requests.
agentic-context-engine.who: Teams running agents in production who want them to learn from past runs.

long: AgentFlow is a trainable agentic system from Stanford in which planner, executor, verifier and generator modules coordinate, with in-the-flow optimization of the system. Our listing notes a Hugging Face demo.
Its paper was accepted at ICLR 2026, and the project was featured at a NeurIPS 2025 workshop.
agentflow.who: Researchers interested in trainable, modular agent systems.
features: Planner, executor, verifier and generator modules

long: IBM CUGA is an enterprise agent harness for sovereign, policy-controlled automation from IBM Research. It turns business requests into actions across your applications, APIs and documents.

You can deploy it in a private cloud or an air-gapped environment, enforce fine-grained execution policies and use open models on infrastructure you control. Our listing notes a live demo on Hugging Face Spaces.
ibm-cuga.who: Enterprises that need agents for web and API tasks under strict policy and data-sovereignty requirements.
features: Requests turned into actions across apps and APIs

long: Lyzr is an enterprise agent studio and framework for building secure AI agents, listed with freemium pricing.
Its open-source Lyzr Automata is a low-code multi-agent framework for process automation; the makers note it began as an experiment and is being improved for stability.
lyzr.who: Enterprises building secure agents, and developers who want a low-code multi-agent automation framework.

long: Viam is a software platform for building and operating robots and smart machines. Its open-source robot architecture exposes robotics functionality through simple APIs.
The core server (RDK) is written in Go, and a cloud platform is offered alongside it.
viam.who: Robotics and hardware teams building and running robots and smart machines.

long: Orca Agent Engine is an open, Apache-2.0, self-hosted implementation of the managed-agents API. You define agents, run them in sessions and stream each session's events.

It follows Anthropic's Managed Agents beta closely enough that the official Anthropic SDKs can use it by changing their base URL, while agents, sessions, files, memory and credentials stay in your infrastructure. Our listing notes a choice of harness (Claude Agent SDK, Codex, Pi) and a Developer Preview released Oct 6, 2026.
orca-agent-engine.who: Teams who want managed-agent style APIs but need to run them on their own infrastructure.
features: Compatible with Anthropic SDKs via base URL

long: Agentset is an open-source platform for building AI apps that give reliable answers from your documents, with production-grade RAG in minutes and no RAG expertise needed.
The company cites benchmark results on MultiHopQA and FinanceBench, and says it works natively with images. A hosted cloud is available.
agentset.who: Developers who want accurate chat and search over their documents without building a RAG pipeline themselves.

long: Mastra is a TypeScript framework for building AI-powered applications and agents, from prototypes to production. It includes agents, workflows and RAG.
It integrates with React, Next.js and Node, or deploys anywhere as a standalone server.
mastra.who: TypeScript developers building agents and AI features into web apps.
features: Works with React, Next.js and Node

long: The Vercel AI SDK is a provider-agnostic TypeScript toolkit for building AI-powered applications and agents with frameworks such as Next.js, React, Svelte, Vue and Angular and runtimes like Node.js.

A unified API works with providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google; by default it uses the Vercel AI Gateway so you can pass a model string for any supported model. It needs Node.js 22+, and an AI SDK skill is offered for coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor.
vercel-ai-sdk.who: TypeScript and JavaScript developers adding chat, generation and agents to web apps.
features: Works with Next.js, React, Svelte, Vue and Angular

long: REA is an MCP server and CLI that lets coding agents reverse-engineer native binaries, Electron and JavaScript apps, .NET assemblies and live websites, using Ghidra, Hopper or IDA under the hood.
Its pitch is that if you see a feature you like in an app, you can understand how it works down to the binary level. The README warns that only its official sources should be trusted for downloads.
rea.who: Security researchers and developers who want agent help with reverse engineering.
features: One MCP server for reverse engineering

long: MCP reference servers is the official repository of reference implementations for the Model Context Protocol, maintained by the MCP steering group, along with pointers to community servers and resources.
It holds only a small number of reference servers; for a full list of servers the README points to the MCP Registry.
mcp-reference-servers.who: Developers learning MCP or looking for canonical example servers to build from.
features: Maintained by the MCP steering group

long: Mem0 is a memory layer for AI agents. Its current algorithm uses single-pass, add-only extraction (one LLM call; memories accumulate and nothing is overwritten), treats agent-generated facts as first-class and links entities across memories for retrieval.
It is open source with a paid managed platform; Mem0 notes its published benchmarks reflect the managed platform, which includes optimizations not in the open-source SDK.
mem0.who: Developers who want agents to remember users and facts across sessions.

long: Context7, from Upstash, is an MCP server and platform that feeds coding agents up-to-date, version-specific library documentation and code examples straight from the source.
That avoids outdated examples and hallucinated APIs that come from old training data, without switching tabs. It is listed as freemium.
context7.who: Developers whose coding agents keep using outdated library APIs.

long: Hindsight, from Vectorize, is an agent memory system built so agents learn over time, not just recall conversation history.
The makers say it overcomes shortcomings of RAG and knowledge-graph approaches and publish benchmarks and a paper. A hosted Hindsight Cloud is available.
hindsight.who: Developers who want agents that improve from experience.

long: LocalAI is an open-source AI engine for running LLM, vision, voice, image and video models on any hardware, no GPU required, with an OpenAI-compatible API.
It has a small core: each backend wraps an engine such as llama.cpp, vLLM, whisper.cpp, stable-diffusion or MLX in its own image, pulled only when a model needs it.
localai.who: Developers and self-hosters who want to run models, and agents on top of them, on their own hardware.
features: LLM, vision, voice, image and video

long: Codebase Memory MCP is a local MCP server that gives Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents a persistent code knowledge graph. It indexes functions, classes, imports, HTTP routes and their relationships.
You can search code, follow call graphs and explore architecture in your browser, and the project aims to cut token usage for agents.
codebase-memory-mcp.who: Developers who want coding agents to look up code structure quickly instead of reading many files.

long: The GitHub MCP Server is GitHub's official MCP server. It connects AI tools to GitHub so agents, assistants and chatbots can read repositories and code, manage issues and pull requests, analyze code and automate workflows in natural language.
Repository features include browsing and querying code, searching files, analyzing commits and understanding project structure across repositories you have access to.
github-mcp-server.who: Developers who want their AI tools to work directly with GitHub repos, issues, PRs and Actions.

long: Cognee is a free, open-source AI memory platform that gives agents persistent long-term memory across sessions. It turns documents, code and conversations into a self-hosted knowledge graph your agents can search and reuse.
The project says it relies on free small models that run on your CPU, and it has published a research paper on knowledge graphs and LLMs. A cloud option is available.
cognee.who: Developers who want self-hosted, graph-based long-term memory for agents.
features: Knowledge graph from documents, code and chats
Runs on CPU with small models

long: Graphiti, from Zep, is a framework for building and querying temporal context graphs for AI agents. Unlike static knowledge graphs, it tracks how facts change over time.
It serves as real-time memory for agents.
graphiti.who: Developers building agents that need memory of facts and relationships that change over time.

long: Google Workspace CLI (gws) is one CLI for all of Google Workspace, built for humans and AI agents: Drive, Gmail, Calendar and every Workspace API, with structured JSON output and 40+ agent skills.
It reads Google's Discovery Service at runtime to build its commands dynamically. Its README states it is not an officially supported Google product.
google-workspace-cli.who: Developers and agents that need to automate Google Workspace from the command line.
features: Drive, Gmail, Calendar and all Workspace APIs
Commands built from Google's Discovery Service

long: Serena is an MCP toolkit that gives coding agents semantic code retrieval, editing, refactoring and debugging tools akin to an IDE's, working at the symbol level.
It integrates with any client or LLM via MCP, and its agent-first tool design uses high-level abstractions rather than line numbers.
serena.who: Developers who want coding agents to navigate and edit code by symbols, like an IDE.

long: Chroma is open-source data infrastructure for AI, widely used as a vector database for agent memory and RAG. Its core API is only four functions.
Chroma Cloud, the hosted service, offers serverless vector, hybrid and full-text search, with $5 of free credits to start.
chroma.who: Developers who need a simple vector store for RAG or agent memory.

long: TencentDB-Agent-Memory is a team-level memory hub that turns conversations, docs and code into shared memory for agents. It runs as three services: memory-core, memory-hub and a proxy.
Its Team Memory feature is in beta, and the docs cover use with Claude Code and CodeBuddy.
tencentdb-agent-memory.who: Teams who want their agents to share memory rather than each starting from scratch.
features: Works with Claude Code and CodeBuddy

long: FastMCP is a Pythonic framework for MCP servers, clients and interactive apps. A server starts with ordinary Python, and declaring a tool as a Python function generates its schema, validation and documentation automatically.
Connecting to a server takes a URL, with transport handled for you. It is maintained by Prefect.
fastmcp.who: Python developers building MCP servers or clients quickly.
features: MCP servers from plain Python functions

long: The MCP Python SDK is the official Python implementation of the Model Context Protocol, for building MCP servers and clients. It is MIT-licensed.
Its docs include a getting-started guide, what's new in v2, an API reference and a migration guide.
mcp-python-sdk.who: Python developers implementing MCP servers or clients against the official SDK.

long: n8n-MCP is an MCP server that gives AI assistants such as Claude and Cursor detailed access to n8n node documentation, properties and operations, so they can build n8n workflows for you.
Its README cites coverage of 3,135 n8n workflow automation nodes (840 core and 2,295 community).
n8n-mcp.who: n8n users who want an AI assistant to design and build workflows.
features: Knowledge of n8n nodes and properties
Works with Claude, Cursor and other MCP clients

long: MCP Toolbox for Databases is Google's open-source MCP server that connects AI agents, IDEs and applications to enterprise databases.
Prebuilt generic tools let clients such as Gemini CLI, Google Antigravity, Claude Code and Codex talk to your data, explore schemas and generate code without boilerplate.
mcp-toolbox-for-databases.who: Developers and data teams who want agents to query and work with their databases safely.
features: Works with Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Codex and more

long: NVIDIA OpenShell is a safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents. It lets agents read files, install packages, call APIs and use credentials without unrestricted access to your data, secrets or network.
Policies are declared in YAML for file, network and credential access. Version 0.1.x brought a stable release cadence, new isolation primitives and new APIs. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.
nvidia-openshell.who: Teams running autonomous agents who need strict, declarative control over what they can touch.
features: YAML policies for files, network and credentials

long: OpenSandbox runs AI agents in sandboxes on your own infrastructure. It gives AI applications isolated environments to execute code, run commands, manage files and operate browsers or desktops.
You start locally with Docker and deploy on Kubernetes through one sandbox API; examples need Python 3.10+.
opensandbox.who: Developers who need secure, self-hosted code execution for agents.
features: Isolated code, command and file execution

long: Corsair is a product integration platform for connecting your users' apps to agents and services. Unlike MCP-only tools, it is built on a REST API, so the same integration layer serves agents, backend services and customer dashboards.
You can build anything from an agent working across your integrations to a multi-tenant dashboard where users connect their accounts.
corsair.who: Product teams who need third-party integrations usable by both their agents and their app.
features: Works for agents, backends and dashboards

long: Casdoor is an open-source, self-hosted identity and access management platform: a single sign-on and authentication server with a web console. Our listing describes it as agent-first, with an MCP and agent gateway.
It speaks OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML 2.0, CAS, LDAP, SCIM 2.0, WebAuthn, TOTP/MFA and MCP, and connects to identity providers such as Google Workspace, Microsoft Entra ID and GitHub.
casdoor.who: Teams that need self-hosted SSO and access control for users and agents.
features: OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, LDAP, SCIM, WebAuthn
Connects to Google, Entra ID and GitHub

long: The MCP TypeScript SDK is the official TypeScript SDK for building MCP servers and clients. Its main branch is v2 (@modelcontextprotocol/server and @modelcontextprotocol/client), implementing the 2026-07-28 MCP spec.
The v1.x line (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk) continues to get bug fixes and security updates for at least six months after the v2 release, and a migration guide is available.
mcp-typescript-sdk.who: TypeScript developers implementing MCP servers or clients.

long: EverOS is a Python library and local-first memory runtime that gives agents one portable memory layer across coding assistants, apps, devices and workflows.
It stores conversations, files and agent trajectories as readable Markdown that you can edit, diff and version in Git, and syncs local SQLite and LanceDB indexes for retrieval.
everos.who: Developers who want agent memory they can read, edit and version as plain files.

long: CubeSandbox, from Tencent Cloud, is a secure sandbox service for AI agents built on RustVMM and KVM, deployable on a single node or as a multi-node cluster.
It is compatible with the E2B SDK, and the README says it can create a hardware-isolated sandbox in under 60 ms with less than 5 MB of memory overhead. Version 0.7 added cross-node pause and resume.
cubesandbox.who: Teams who need fast, hardware-isolated sandboxes for agent code at scale.

long: IDA Pro MCP is a simple MCP server that connects IDA Pro to language models for AI-assisted reverse engineering. It needs IDA Pro 8.3 or higher.
Its author now recommends the official Hex-Rays IDA MCP Server instead.
ida-pro-mcp.who: Reverse engineers using IDA Pro who want LLM assistance; consider the official Hex-Rays server first.
features: Connects IDA Pro to LLMs via MCP

long: MemOS is a memory operating system for LLMs and AI agents that unifies storing, retrieving and managing memory, giving agents persistent memory and the ability to grow.
It can connect to DeepSeek Harness, adding automatic recall, background capture, hybrid retrieval and a local Memory Viewer.
memos.who: Developers who want a full memory system for agents.

long: CocoIndex is an incremental data engine that turns codebases, meeting notes, inboxes, Slack, PDFs and videos into live, continuously fresh context for AI agents and LLM apps.
It processes only what changed, runs in parallel by default and is declarative in Python.
cocoindex.who: Teams whose agents need context that stays current as source data changes.
features: Many sources: code, notes, email, Slack, PDFs, video

long: LanceDB is an open-source multimodal vector database for fast, scalable vector search, built on the Lance columnar format. It can store, index and search petabytes of multimodal data and vectors.
It is used for search, RAG and agent memory, and a cloud option is available.
lancedb.who: Developers storing and searching embeddings and multimodal data for RAG or agents.

long: The Apify MCP Server, at mcp.apify.com, lets AI agents extract data from social media, search engines, maps, e-commerce sites and other websites using thousands of ready-made scrapers, crawlers and automation tools from Apify Store.
It supports OAuth, so you can connect from clients like Claude.ai or VS Code with just the URL.
apify-mcp-server.who: Developers who want agents to collect web data without writing scrapers.
features: Social, search, maps and e-commerce data

long: mcp-use is a full-stack MCP framework for building, testing and shipping MCP servers, ChatGPT plugins, Claude connectors and agents that connect to them.
It is fully typed with Zod schemas flowing from tools to results, supports native Views and MCP Apps that bind React views to tools, and includes a built-in Inspector.
mcp-use.who: Developers building MCP servers and interactive MCP apps.

long: Electric is a Postgres sync engine that handles partial replication, fan-out and data delivery, syncing data out of Postgres into apps and agents in real time.
Our listing describes it as a sync engine and agent platform for keeping data in sync between Postgres, apps and agents. A cloud option is available.
electric.who: Developers building fast local-first apps or agents that work on live Postgres data.
features: Real-time data for apps and agents

long: Bindu is an identity, communication and payments layer for AI agents, so agents can talk to each other, prove who they are and get paid for their work.
Its README describes a Gmail-shaped inbox for the agent internet, where agents send signed JSON-RPC messages to each other and identities are verified inline.
bindu.who: Developers who want their agents to interact with, authenticate to and transact with other agents.

long: AWS MCP Servers is a suite of official open-source MCP servers from AWS Labs that help you work with AWS services wherever you use MCP.
AWS notes that the new Agent Toolkit for AWS is now the successor to these MCP servers, plugins and skills, so check it for production work.
aws-mcp-servers.who: Developers and agents working with AWS through MCP clients.
features: Specialized MCP servers for AWS services

long: Replicate lets you run and deploy open models through an API with usage-based pricing. Its open-source tool Cog packages machine-learning models in standard, production-ready containers.
With Cog you define the environment in a simple config file instead of writing your own Dockerfile, then deploy the model to your own infrastructure or to Replicate.
replicate.who: Developers who want to call or deploy open models via an API without managing GPUs.
features: Cog for packaging models in containers
Deploy to Replicate or your own infrastructure

long: Nasiko is an open runtime for agents, coding harnesses, frameworks and tools. It finds the coding agents already running in an organization, shows what each costs by harness and model, and routes them to the models you choose.
Developers keep using their existing harness workflows while the organization gets visibility and control.
nasiko.who: Engineering leaders who want visibility and model control over the coding agents their developers already use.

long: Activeloop makes Deep Lake, a database for AI built on a storage format optimized for deep learning. It stores data plus vectors, including embeddings, images, text and video, for LLM apps and RAG.
It is also used to manage datasets while training deep-learning models. A cloud offering is available.
activeloop.who: Teams building RAG or multimodal AI apps and managing training datasets.
features: Multimodal storage: vectors, images, text, video

long: microsandbox runs untrusted workloads, such as AI agents, user code, plugins, CI jobs and scrapers, inside fast, local microVMs with hardware-level isolation.
You can fork live sandboxes and snapshot running ones.
microsandbox.who: Developers who need to run agent or user code safely on their own machines.

long: GitMCP is a free, open-source remote MCP server that turns any GitHub project, repositories or GitHub Pages, into a documentation hub for AI tools like Cursor.
That lets agents access up-to-date docs and code even for projects the model has never seen, reducing hallucinated APIs.
gitmcp.who: Developers whose coding agents need accurate docs for less-known or fast-moving libraries.
features: Remote MCP for any GitHub repo

long: Honcho, from Plastic Labs, is memory infrastructure for stateful agents that understand changing people, agents, groups, projects and ideas over time.

You store messages and events, Honcho reasons over them in the background, and you query peer representations, session context, search results or insights from any model or framework. It runs managed at api.honcho.dev or locally.
honcho.who: Developers building agents that need to remember and understand their users over time.
features: Works with any model or framework

long: Reef is open-source infrastructure for continually self-improving agents. It connects agent inference, feedback, learning and versioned delivery.
You can use it to train model weights with Slime and SGLang, or to improve an agent's harness, including its prompts, rules and skills.
reef.who: ML teams who want agents that keep improving from feedback in production.
features: Weight training via Slime and SGLang

long: BrowserTools MCP gives AI coding agents eyes on the browser. It streams console output, network activity, screenshots and Lighthouse audits from your real Chrome session to MCP clients such as Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, Cline, Zed and Gemini CLI.
Version 2.0 is a rewrite that runs as one process.
browsertools-mcp.who: Web developers who want their coding agent to see browser errors and network calls while debugging.

long: Talk to Figma MCP, from Grab, is an MCP integration between AI agents such as Cursor or Claude Code and Figma, letting the agent read designs and modify them programmatically.
It includes a TypeScript MCP server for the Figma integration.
talk-to-figma-mcp.who: Designers and developers who want an agent to inspect or edit Figma files.
features: Works with Cursor and Claude Code

long: smolvm embeds lightweight virtual machines into your software for portable dev environments and local sandboxing, so agents can run safely on your computer.
It runs on Windows (with the Windows Hypervisor Platform) and other platforms, and its docs are written for both humans and coding agents.
smolvm.who: Developers who want branchable, portable VMs for running agents locally.

long: Open Connector is an open-source connector gateway for AI agents and an alternative to Pipedream or Composio. Users connect app accounts once, and agents get a shared catalog of 1,000+ providers.
There is a managed option with hosted OAuth and runtime, or you can run it yourself with Docker or Node.js and manage storage and OAuth. Our listing notes access via SDK, CLI and MCP.
open-connector.who: Developers who need agents to act in users' SaaS accounts without building auth for each app.

long: Lemonade is a local AI server that offers capabilities similar to cloud APIs, free and private, running the latest models for chat, coding, speech and image generation on your own NPU and GPU.
Lemonade Server connects to many apps through standard OpenAI, Anthropic and Ollama APIs, and an embeddable version is available.
lemonade.who: People and developers who want to run AI models and agents locally on their own hardware.
features: Local LLM, speech and image models

long: Klavis AI provides MCP integrations for agents, with 100+ prebuilt integrations and OAuth support, designed to use tools reliably and optimize the context window.
The company also provides live, real-world MCP environments for training agents with long-horizon tool-use data, used by AI labs.
klavis-ai.who: Developers connecting agents to many tools, and labs training agents on tool use.
features: MCP environments for training and RL

long: Wigolo is local-first web search, fetch and crawl for AI agents over MCP, with no API keys, no cloud and no metered bill.
It works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, VS Code, Windsurf, Zed and more, plus frameworks like LangChain, CrewAI, LlamaIndex and the Vercel AI SDK, or plain REST.
wigolo.who: Developers who want web access for agents without paying for a search API.
features: Works with many agents and frameworks

long: Zotero MCP connects your Zotero research library to Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor and other assistants, so you can search, read, cite and annotate your papers.
It also offers a chat panel inside Zotero, with page citations that open the cited passage.
zotero-mcp.who: Researchers and students who manage papers in Zotero.
features: Search, read, cite and annotate papers
Works with Claude, ChatGPT, Codex and Cursor

long: agentgateway is an open-source proxy built on AI-native protocols (MCP and A2A) that adds security, observability and governance to agent-to-LLM, agent-to-tool and agent-to-agent traffic across frameworks and environments.
It routes traffic to major LLM providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Bedrock.
agentgateway.who: Platform teams who need to secure and observe agent traffic.

long: Olares is an open-source personal cloud OS you operate in plain language, built to run AI agents and LLMs on hardware you own.
Powered by Kubernetes, it turns your machines into a self-hosted AI platform reachable from any browser, with compute, storage, networking and apps in one place.
olares.who: Individuals and small teams who want always-on agents and models at home or on their own servers.
features: Runs agents and LLMs on your hardware

long: ACI.dev is an open-source tool-calling platform that connects 600+ tools to agentic IDEs or custom agents, with intent-aware tool access and multi-tenant auth.
A separate Unified MCP server is built on the platform. A cloud option is available.
aci-dev.who: Developers who want many tools available to their agents through one platform.

long: Liveblocks provides building blocks and infrastructure that let people and AI work together inside your app, with realtime collaboration features.
Its products include pre-built hooks, components and APIs that you can use individually or together. It is listed as paid.
liveblocks.who: Product teams adding multiplayer collaboration and AI agents to their apps.

long: ContextForge is IBM's open-source registry and proxy that federates MCP, A2A and REST/gRPC APIs into one endpoint for AI clients.
It provides centralized governance, discovery and observability, optimizes agent and tool calls, and supports plugins.
contextforge.who: Enterprises managing many tools and agents who want one governed gateway.
features: Federates MCP, A2A, REST and gRPC

long: The MCP C# SDK is the official C# SDK for the Model Context Protocol, letting .NET applications, services and libraries implement MCP clients and servers.
It ships packages such as ModelContextProtocol.Core for projects that only need client or low-level server APIs. Our listing notes it is maintained with Microsoft.
mcp-c-sdk.who: .NET developers building MCP servers or clients.

long: nono is an agent runtime security tool that secures agents, their tools, their credentials and the skills and instructions they follow, with low latency.
Our listing describes it as zero-trust sandboxing for agent runtimes. The project is approaching 1.0 and says APIs are stabilizing.
nono.who: Teams running agents who need to lock down tools, credentials and instructions.

long: Judge0 is a robust, scalable, sandboxed open-source online code execution system for humans and AI. It can power applications such as AI agents that need to run code.
A hosted option is available alongside the open-source system.
judge0.who: Developers who need to run untrusted code from users or agents safely.

long: Unity MCP is an AI-powered game-development assistant for the Unity Editor and runtime. It connects Claude, Cursor and Windsurf to Unity via MCP to automate workflows and generate code.
Unlike editor-only tools, it can also work inside your compiled game, enabling real-time AI debugging and player-AI interaction.
unity-mcp.who: Unity developers who want AI agents to help build, test and debug games.
features: Works with Claude, Cursor and Windsurf

long: mcpo, from Open WebUI, is a simple proxy that takes an MCP server command and exposes it as a standard RESTful OpenAPI server.
That way MCP tools work with LLM agents and apps that expect OpenAPI, and gain standard features such as docs that raw stdio MCP servers lack.
mcpo.who: Developers who want to use MCP tools from OpenAPI-based apps such as Open WebUI.

long: AntV MCP Server Chart is a TypeScript MCP server from AntV for chart generation and data analysis. Our listing notes it supports more than 25 chart types.
It exposes chart types as MCP tools, such as area charts, and can also be used in Dify.
antv-mcp-server-chart.who: Developers and analysts who want agents to produce charts from data.

long: Cloudflare MCP Servers is a collection of MCP servers that connect MCP clients like Cursor and Claude to Cloudflare services, so you can use natural language to work with your Cloudflare account.
Our listing notes coverage of Workers, observability, DNS analytics and other Cloudflare services.
cloudflare-mcp-servers.who: Developers who manage Cloudflare resources and want to do it through an AI assistant.
features: Works with Cursor, Claude and other clients

long: Archestra is an all-in-one open-source enterprise AI platform with guardrails, an MCP registry, a gateway and an orchestrator.
It is built on security and observability: SSO and RBAC, sandboxed code execution, Lethal-Trifecta guardrails, OpenTelemetry traces and Prometheus metrics. A cloud option is available.
archestra.who: Enterprises rolling out agents and MCP tools that need governance and security.

long: optillm is an OpenAI API-compatible optimizing inference proxy that applies 20+ reasoning techniques to improve LLM accuracy on reasoning tasks without training or fine-tuning.
Its README claims 2-10x accuracy improvements on reasoning tasks.
optillm.who: Developers who want better reasoning from existing models by changing only the endpoint.

long: Excel MCP Server is an open-source MCP server that lets Claude, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, Codex and other clients create, read and edit Excel files, including charts, PivotTables, formulas and tables.
It is built on openpyxl, needs no Microsoft Excel, and runs on Windows, macOS and Linux.
excel-mcp-server.who: People who want AI assistants to build or update spreadsheets.
features: Create, read and edit Excel files

long: ArcBox is a fast, open-source container and VM runtime for macOS, written from scratch in Rust, with drop-in Docker support and agent sandboxes.
It positions itself as an open-source (MIT/Apache-2.0) alternative to Docker Desktop and OrbStack. Our listing notes it runs agents on isolated machines with their own kernel, filesystem and network.
arcbox.who: Mac developers who want fast containers and isolated sandboxes for agents.
features: Container and VM runtime for macOS

long: The MCP Rust SDK is the official Rust implementation of the Model Context Protocol, built on the tokio async runtime.
It includes the rmcp core crate and rmcp-macros for generating tools, and a migration guide covers the 3.x breaking changes.
mcp-rust-sdk.who: Rust developers building MCP servers or clients.

long: LinkedIn MCP Server gives AI agents access to LinkedIn through your own browser session: read profiles, research companies, find jobs, and manage conversations and connection requests.
It is an independent open-source project, not affiliated with LinkedIn or Microsoft.
linkedin-mcp-server.who: People who want an assistant to help with LinkedIn research and job search.

long: Radar is an open-source Kubernetes UI with a built-in MCP server for AI agents. It is a single binary that needs no account and is free, and it can run from your laptop or in-cluster.
Views include topology, resources, Helm, GitOps, traffic, cost, audit, RBAC and upgrade impact, with nothing to install on the cluster.
radar.who: Kubernetes users who want a visual UI plus cluster context for their AI agents.
features: Helm, GitOps, traffic and cost views

long: The Azure MCP Server is Microsoft's MCP server for connecting AI agents and assistants to Azure services.
It lives in Microsoft's MCP repository, which explains MCP's client-server architecture of hosts, clients and servers.
azure-mcp-server.who: Developers and teams working with Azure who want AI assistants to act on their resources.

long: The MCP Java SDK is the official set of Java projects for the Model Context Protocol. It lets Java applications interact with AI models and tools through a standard interface.
It supports both synchronous and asynchronous communication patterns.
mcp-java-sdk.who: Java developers building MCP servers or clients.

long: Acontext is an open-source skill memory layer for AI agents. It automatically captures learnings from agent runs and stores them as agent skill files you can read, edit and share across agents, LLMs and frameworks.
The aim is for agents to learn from mistakes and reuse what worked without opaque memory polluting the context.
acontext.who: Developers who want agent learnings stored as readable, shareable skills.

long: Mirage is a virtual terminal for AI agents. A virtual filesystem provides broad data context, virtualized CLIs give agents flexible tool use, and dynamic runtimes save infrastructure cost and tokens.
Fine-grained control over what the agent can do and see is part of its security model.
mirage.who: Developers who want agents to work in a controlled, virtual terminal environment.

long: DBHub, from Bytebase, is a minimal database MCP server: token-efficient, zero-dependency, with just two tools by default and opt-in extras. Our listing notes support for Postgres, MySQL, SQL Server and others.
Bytebase points to its main product for enterprise needs such as approval flows, access control, data masking and audit logging.
dbhub.who: Developers who want agents to explore and query databases with minimal overhead.

long: ReMe, from the AgentScope team, is a local-first, self-evolving personal knowledge base for AI agents. It turns conversations and resources into readable, editable, searchable and interconnected Markdown memory.
Agents such as QwenPaw and DeepSeek Harness can share the same workspace to retrieve, maintain and evolve knowledge.
reme.who: Developers who want agent memory stored as ordinary, editable files.

long: OneCLI is an open-source platform for running AI agents as a team in a company: you create a sandboxed personal agent for each employee and give each one only the access it needs.
Agents work in a sandbox and are routed through a gateway that handles credentials securely. It can be installed on Kubernetes with a Helm chart.
onecli.who: Companies that want to give every employee a secure, sandboxed AI agent.

long: DaVinci Resolve MCP is an MCP server that lets AI assistants control DaVinci Resolve Studio through its official Scripting API.
It provides full API coverage plus guarded helpers for editing, media-pool organization, render setup, review markers, grading, Fusion, Fairlight and project tasks.
davinci-resolve-mcp.who: Video editors who want an AI assistant to automate DaVinci Resolve work.

long: Grafana MCP is Grafana's MCP server, giving AI agents access to your Grafana instance and its ecosystem. Our listing notes dashboards, data sources and incidents.
It requires uv and is configured in MCP clients such as Claude Desktop or Cursor; it also works with Grafana Cloud.
grafana-mcp.who: SRE and ops teams who want AI assistants to query Grafana.

long: AgentFS, from Turso, is a filesystem designed for AI agents, providing the storage abstractions agents need the way traditional filesystems serve applications. Our listing notes snapshots and auditing.
It is in beta, and the README advises caution and backups with production data.
agentfs.who: Developers who want agent file activity to be snapshotted and auditable.

long: arXiv MCP Server is a local MCP server for agent literature work. It reads original-LaTeX sections, generates BibTeX from arXiv metadata and supports topic watches, with papers kept on disk.
The working loop is paper ID, outline, one section, then citations; search is optional. The default install is uvx arxiv-mcp-server.
arxiv-mcp-server.who: Researchers who want an AI assistant to read and cite arXiv papers.

long: seekdb, from OceanBase, is an AI-native search database and state store for AI agents. It is MySQL-compatible, runs embedded or as a server, and combines vector, full-text and scalar search in one SQL query.
It has full ACID transactions, fork-and-merge copy-on-write sandboxes for safe agent exploration, and works with LangChain, LlamaIndex and Dify.
seekdb.who: Developers who need one database for agent state, vectors and text search.
features: Hybrid vector and full-text search in SQL

long: MemMachine is an open-source long-term memory layer for AI agents and LLM apps, so they can learn, store and recall information from past sessions.
The project says you can add persistent memory with about five lines of code.
memmachine.who: Developers turning stateless chatbots into personalized agents.

long: Supabase MCP connects your Supabase projects to Cursor, Claude, Windsurf and other AI assistants.
Assistants can manage tables, fetch configuration and query data, among other tools.
supabase-mcp.who: Supabase users who want an AI assistant to manage their database and project.
features: Works with Cursor, Claude and Windsurf

long: mcp-proxy is a tool for switching between MCP server transports, bridging Streamable HTTP or SSE and stdio.

In one mode it runs a stdio proxy that connects to a remote SSE server, so clients like Claude Desktop can talk to remote servers even where that transport is not supported natively; another mode exposes a local stdio server over the network.
mcp-proxy.who: Developers connecting MCP clients and servers that use different transports.

long: jCodeMunch MCP is an MCP server for precise, symbol-level source-code retrieval using tree-sitter AST parsing, so agents stop reading entire files.
Its README reports 86-99% lower token use on code exploration (96% on average) versus a grep-and-read agent.
jcodemunch-mcp.who: Developers who want coding agents to explore code with far fewer tokens.

long: MetaMCP is an MCP aggregator, orchestrator, middleware and gateway in one Docker image, combining many MCP servers into one.
The maintainers note active development on an ai-dev branch and advise testing before building images from it.
metamcp.who: Developers and teams who run many MCP servers and want one endpoint.

long: Bright Data MCP is Bright Data's MCP server for web search, page scraping, structured data extraction and browser automation for AI agents and LLMs.
It works with any MCP-compatible client and has a free tier of 5,000 requests per month with no credit card required.
bright-data-mcp.who: Developers whose agents need reliable access to web data.

long: MCPHub is an open-source, self-hosted MCP gateway and control plane for connecting, controlling and operating MCP servers.
You connect local and remote servers once, organize and route their capabilities through stable endpoints, and control access with authentication.
mcphub.who: Teams managing many MCP servers for many AI clients.

long: NitroStack is a TypeScript framework for building production-ready MCP servers, with decorators, dependency injection and widgets.
Once your project is scaffolded you can open it in NitroStudio, a companion desktop app, for visual testing.
nitrostack.who: TypeScript developers building MCP servers and MCP apps.

long: BoxLite is an embeddable micro-VM for AI agents, light enough for a laptop and elastic enough for an agentic cloud. Each Box is a hardware-isolated micro-VM that runs any OCI image.
Boxes persist, so agents can install packages, write files and resume across turns without starting cold, and each has its own kernel for stronger isolation than containers.
boxlite.who: Developers who need persistent, isolated compute for agents.

long: The Figma MCP Server brings Figma into your workflow by giving AI agents design information and context when they generate code from Figma design files.
Rate limits apply to tools that read data from Figma, while some tools that write to Figma files are exempt.
figma-mcp-server.who: Developers turning Figma designs into code with an AI agent.

long: Stripe's agent toolkit is a one-stop repo for building AI-powered products on Stripe, with SDKs to integrate Stripe with LLMs and agent frameworks.
It includes, for example, @stripe/ai-sdk for Vercel's AI SDK and @stripe/token-meter for billing on token usage. Our listing notes an MCP server for customers, payments and billing.
stripe-agent-toolkit.who: Developers who want agents to work with Stripe payments and billing.
features: SDKs for LLMs and agent frameworks

long: Microsoft Learn MCP is Microsoft's official MCP server giving AI assistants such as Claude, Cursor, Copilot and Codex direct access to the latest official Microsoft documentation.
It is free with one-click install and no key needed.
microsoft-learn-mcp.who: Developers working with Microsoft technologies who want accurate, current docs in their agent.

long: pg-aiguide, from Timescale, helps AI coding tools write better PostgreSQL code.
It provides version-aware semantic search across the official PostgreSQL manual and curated, opinionated Postgres best-practice skills that agents use automatically.
pg-aiguide.who: Developers whose agents write SQL and schemas for Postgres.

long: The MATLAB MCP Server is MathWorks' official MCP server for running MATLAB from AI applications. It can, for example, assess your MATLAB code for style and correctness.
MathWorks also offers MATLAB and Simulink Agentic Toolkits with skills for agents.
matlab-mcp-server.who: MATLAB and Simulink users who want AI agents to run and check their code.

long: Testkube is an open testing platform for defining, running and analyzing automated tests with your existing testing tools and scripts, running in your Kubernetes infrastructure.
Its MCP server lets agents manage test workflows and executions.
testkube-mcp.who: Engineering teams running automated tests on Kubernetes.
features: Run existing test tools in Kubernetes

long: The Terraform MCP Server, from HashiCorp, integrates with the Terraform Registry and HCP Terraform APIs for infrastructure-as-code automation.
Our listing notes it helps agents look up providers and modules and automate workflows; the README lists clients such as Claude Desktop, Amazon Q Developer and Kiro CLI.
terraform-mcp-server.who: Infrastructure engineers using AI assistants with Terraform.

long: Brave Search MCP is Brave's official MCP server for the Brave Search API, with web, local business, place, image, video and news search, LLM context and AI summarization.
It supports STDIO and HTTP transports, with STDIO as the default.
brave-search-mcp.who: Developers who want independent web search in their agents.
features: Web, image, video and news search

long: ROS MCP Server connects language models such as Claude, GPT and Gemini to robots running ROS, with two-way communication: models can control robots and read their state.
It requires no changes to robot source code; you add the rosbridge node to your existing ROS setup.
ros-mcp-server.who: Robotics developers who want to control ROS robots with an LLM.

long: SearXNG MCP is an MCP server that gives AI assistants privacy-respecting web search through a SearXNG instance you control or trust, with Claude, Cursor and more.
You need an existing SearXNG instance with JSON search enabled.
searxng-mcp.who: People who want private web search for their AI assistant.

long: Power BI Modeling MCP is Microsoft's MCP server for creating and editing Power BI semantic models with AI agents.
Microsoft recommends its remote, hosted Power BI Authoring MCP server when authoring in a Fabric workspace, since it needs no local install.
power-bi-modeling-mcp.who: Power BI developers who want an agent to build or modify semantic models.
features: Local server; hosted option for Fabric

long: Ref is an MCP server that gives AI coding tools access to documentation for APIs, services and libraries, keeping agents up to date in a fast, token-efficient way.
Its tools are designed to match how models search, returning just the right context. It is listed as freemium.
ref.who: Developers whose coding agents need accurate, current documentation.

long: MongoDB MCP Server is MongoDB's official MCP server for working with MongoDB databases and MongoDB Atlas.
It comes bundled with official MongoDB plugins for AI agents, including one that connects to the hosted Atlas MCP server.
mongodb-mcp-server.who: Developers using MongoDB who want agents to query data or manage Atlas.

long: The Atlassian Rovo MCP Server is Atlassian's official, cloud-hosted MCP server giving AI tools secure, real-time access to Jira, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Bitbucket, Compass, Loom and more.
It is powered by your Teamwork Graph. It is listed as freemium.
atlassian-rovo-mcp-server.who: Teams on Atlassian Cloud who want AI agents to work with Jira and Confluence.
features: Jira, Confluence, JSM, Bitbucket, Compass and Loom

long: Neo4j MCP is a set of MCP servers from the Neo4j Labs program, maintained by the Neo4j Field GenAI team, for querying graphs, managing Aura instances and graph memory.
They are actively developed with experimental features and are not supported by the Neo4j product team.
neo4j-mcp.who: Developers using Neo4j who want agents to query graphs or use them as memory.

long: ClickHouse MCP is the official MCP server for querying and exploring ClickHouse databases.
It implements the 2026-07-28 MCP spec and still supports legacy handshakes for older clients.
clickhouse-mcp.who: Analytics teams who want agents to query ClickHouse.
features: Current and legacy MCP protocol support

long: The SonarQube MCP Server integrates SonarQube Server or Cloud with AI agents for code quality and security.
It can also analyze code snippets directly within the agent's context.
sonarqube-mcp-server.who: Teams using SonarQube who want agents to check quality and security issues.

long: Neon MCP Server is an open-source tool that lets you work with your Lakebase Postgres databases on Neon in natural language.
The repository provides a remote MCP server; our listing notes management of projects, branches and queries.
neon-mcp.who: Neon users who want an AI assistant to manage Postgres projects and branches.

long: The Redis MCP Server is Redis' official natural-language interface for agentic applications to manage and search data in Redis.
It integrates with MCP clients so AI workflows can work with structured and unstructured data in Redis.
redis-mcp-server.who: Developers who want agents to read, write and search Redis data.

long: The Anytype MCP Server lets AI assistants interact with Anytype's API through natural language.
It converts Anytype's OpenAPI specification into MCP tools, so you can manage your knowledge base through conversation.
anytype-mcp.who: Anytype users who want an AI assistant to work with their notes and knowledge base.
features: Manage your knowledge base by chat

long: Zapier MCP gives any MCP-compatible AI client governed access to 9,000+ apps, to send messages, pull data and trigger workflows in plain English, with no code or infrastructure.
Zapier says it is SOC 2 Type II certified. The repo distributes the Zapier MCP plugin you install from your client's marketplace. It is listed as freemium.
zapier-mcp.who: People who want their AI assistant to take actions across many business apps.

long: monday.com MCP is monday.com's open framework for connecting AI agents to its work OS, giving them secure access to structured data, tools to take action and context for decisions.
It is maintained by the monday.com AI team; our listing notes management of boards, items and workflows.
monday-com-mcp.who: Teams on monday.com who want agents to manage their boards and workflows.

long: The Postman MCP Server connects AI agents and coding assistants, including Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, GitHub Copilot CLI and Gemini CLI, to your Postman workspaces, collections, specifications and environments.
Postman also offers the server as an npm package.
postman-mcp-server.who: API developers who want their agent to work with Postman collections and specs.

long: The official Hugging Face MCP Server connects your LLM to the Hugging Face Hub and thousands of Gradio AI applications.
You can add it as a connector, for example in Claude's connector settings. Our listing notes access to models, datasets, papers and Spaces.
hugging-face-mcp-server.who: AI developers who want assistants to search and use Hugging Face resources.

long: Mux MCP is Mux's official MCP server for video and the Mux API. It lives alongside Mux's server-side TypeScript/JavaScript SDK for the Mux REST API.
API documentation is on docs.mux.com.
mux-mcp.who: Developers building video features who want agents to work with Mux.

long: Webflow MCP is a Node.js MCP server built on the Webflow JavaScript SDK that lets AI agents interact with Webflow APIs.
A remote MCP server is available that uses OAuth to authenticate with your Webflow sites.
webflow-mcp.who: Webflow users who want an agent to help design and manage sites.

long: The Auth0 MCP Server connects Claude, Cursor or Windsurf to your Auth0 tenant so an agent can create apps, deploy Actions and more.
Our listing notes management of applications, APIs, actions and logs.
auth0-mcp-server.who: Developers who manage Auth0 tenants and want an AI assistant's help.

long: ScrapeGraph MCP is a production-ready MCP server for the ScrapeGraph AI API, giving language models AI-powered web-scraping capabilities.
It targets ScrapeGraph API v2.
scrapegraph-mcp.who: Developers who want agents to extract web data with AI scraping.

long: InfraNodus MCP integrates InfraNodus knowledge-graph and text-network analysis into LLM workflows and AI assistants like Claude Desktop.
It is available on npm.
infranodus-mcp.who: Researchers and writers who want to analyze text structure and gaps with an assistant.

long: The Oxylabs MCP server bridges AI models and the web: it can scrape any URL, render JavaScript-heavy pages, extract and format content for AI and access geo-restricted content.
Oxylabs describes it as one API that delivers clean, structured data from any site.
oxylabs-mcp.who: Developers whose agents need web data at scale.

long: The Upstash MCP server lets your agent manage and debug Upstash resources across Redis, QStash, Workflow and Upstash Box.
Upstash notes that for most workflows it recommends installing the Upstash Skill and letting your agent drive @upstash/cli instead.
upstash-mcp.who: Upstash users who want an agent to manage their resources.
features: Skill + CLI recommended for most workflows

long: Buildkite MCP is Buildkite's MCP server exposing pipelines, builds, jobs and tests to AI tooling and editors.
A retries toolset lets agents investigate failures and retry jobs without broader build-write access. Full docs are at buildkite.com/docs/apis/mcp-server.
buildkite-mcp.who: Teams on Buildkite who want coding agents to debug CI.

long: Linkup MCP provides web search and page fetching through Linkup's API, so assistants like Claude can search with natural-language queries and fetch content from any page.
Our listing describes it as real-time, source-backed web search.
linkup-mcp.who: Developers who want source-backed web search for their agents.

long: The Stack Overflow MCP Server connects your AI to Stack Overflow's community knowledge through MCP, for developers from open-source contributors to small teams experimenting with agents.
Our listing notes it is an official remote server that lets coding agents search and pull vetted questions and answers, with a free daily call allowance per user.
stack-overflow-mcp.who: Developers who want coding agents to draw on Stack Overflow answers.

long: Wix MCP lets you work with Wix tools and services in your AI client: search the Wix documentation, write code for the Wix platform and make API calls on Wix sites.
Our listing notes building and managing Wix sites and business data.
wix-mcp.who: Wix site owners and developers who want an AI assistant's help.
features: Call Wix APIs on your sites

long: The PayPal MCP server integrates PayPal APIs through function calling, with tools for different PayPal services.
It runs via npx with your PayPal access token. Our listing notes invoices, orders and payments.
paypal-mcp.who: Businesses and developers who want agents to handle PayPal operations.

long: PlanetScale MCP is PlanetScale's MCP server for databases, branches, schemas and query insights. The repo holds tool implementations for the hosted server.
The full hosted server includes more tools generated from the PlanetScale API OpenAPI spec. It is listed as freemium.
planetscale-mcp.who: PlanetScale users who want agents to inspect and manage databases.
